# Burke Philosophic-School Mapping

**5 schools × featured pentad term × per-philosopher exegetical move (≥30 philosophers)**

Burke's diagnostic apparatus from *Grammar of Motives* Part 2. Each school is recognized by **which pentad term it features** as motive-locus, not by which terms it uses. The diagnostic is **non-bijective**: pragmatism deploys all five terms while featuring Agency; mysticism deploys all five while featuring Purpose. The dissertation can deploy this on game-design theories.

---

## 1. Materialism — features SCENE (GM-04)

**Diagnostic.** Vocabulary generated by treating Scene as Ausgangspunkt; other pentad terms reduced, slighted, or scenically derived. Narrows the scenic circumference; reduces action to motion; excludes personal/spiritual causes.

| Philosopher | Pages | Burke's exegetical move |
|---|---|---|
| **Hobbes** | 132-137 | Most thorough exemplar of vocabulary on extension. *Leviathan*'s machine-metaphor literalized; sense/imagination/will/passion as motion; will reduced to 'last appetite'; action re-emerges under moral pressure. Scenic signature: mechanism + State-as-gigantic-man. |
| **Spinoza** | 137-152 | Chapter's central interlocutor. *Deus sive Natura* as action=motion; Active/Passive ledger; conatus as scenically-derived agent-equivalent; geometry dramatistically contextual ('all determination is negation'). Bridges theological→naturalistic→idealistic. |
| **Darwin** | 152-159 | Conditions of Existence as materialist higher law. Variability as Janus term where scene overlaps agent. 'Agent-minus' as Grammatical category. Mendelian counterpart points toward Agent-featuring. |
| **Lucretius** | 159-165 | Atomic *clinamen* as 'pre-agentification of scene' — internal swerve giving scenic derivation for human freedom. Goaded materialism; philosophic/poetic identity-clash. |
| **Epicurus** | 160-161 | Source of Lucretian atomism; ataraxia as ethical residue. |
| **Stoicism (Marcus Aurelius, Epictetus, Cleanthes)** | 161 | *Pronoia* as scenic ground endowed with purposive properties = scene-featuring-with-pre-agentification. Straddles materialism and mysticism. |
| **Democritus** | 160 background | Pre-Lucretian atomist background. |

**Characteristic moves.** Body-and-motion Ausgangspunkt · suppression/scenic-derivation of other terms · conatus/variability/clinamen as agent-minus surrogates · action-vocabulary replaced by motion-vocabulary.

**Dissertation game-studies deployment.** Materialism features Scene → applies to environmental-storytelling, level-design-as-determinant frameworks, platform-studies (Bogost on platform constraints). **Test:** does this theory explain motive primarily via the gameworld/platform/affordance-structure?

---

## 2. Idealism — features AGENT (GM-05)

**Diagnostic.** Scene/act/agency/purpose derived from properties of the constituting subject (mind, ego, consciousness, will, spirit, super-agent). The school is recognizable not by which terms it uses but by which it features as ground.

| Philosopher | Pages | Burke's exegetical move |
|---|---|---|
| **Berkeley** | 175-181 | Cleanest idealist exhibit. *Esse* is *percipi*; matter dissolved into ideas; scenic residue routed through God as 'Almighty Agent.' Strategy IS the operationalization of Agent. |
| **Hume** | 181-184 | Transitional. Equates ideas with sensations; dismantles causality/power as empirically un-derivable. The 'great dramatist cluster' begins to fall apart — but the dismantling is agent-featuring (reflects on 'operations of our own minds'). |
| **Leibniz** | 184-187 | Rationalism of idealist cast. Monad as atom-agent with internal self-development; pre-established harmony; God as Monas Monadum. Provides Kant the unification-pressure. |
| **Kant** | 187-200 | Dominant idealism interlocutor. Solves Hume's medium-demand by equating medium with universalized agent: 'the understanding' as locus of categories. Transcendent realm added via Coleridgean desynonymizing of transcendental/transcendent. |
| **Hegel** | 202-204 | World History as development of Spirit; cunning of Reason; State as Divine Idea on earth; World-Historical Hero close to Spirit's fountainhead. |
| **Marx / Engels / Lenin** | 200-215 | HYBRID. Grows out of idealism BY ANTITHESIS (Hegel inverted, matter as prius). Surface materialist; structural motive-locus is class-as-collective-agent. Lenin's property-similar-to-sensation in matter smuggles agenthood into materialist scene. |
| **Fichte** | brief | Post-Kantian radicalization: ego positing non-ego; absolute self-positing. |
| **Schelling** | brief | Nature as visible Spirit; pre-Hegelian transition. |
| **Schopenhauer** | brief | Will as thing-in-itself; pessimistic idealism. |
| **Santayana** | GM-04 + GM-05 p.217 | Materialist-grounded agent retaining transcendent function; spirit as moral fruition of physical life. |

**Characteristic moves.** Esse is percipi · super-agent (God, Spirit, Nation-Will, Class-Consciousness) · universalized agent as transcendental medium · cunning of Reason · collective agent (class, party, race).

**Dissertation game-studies deployment.** Idealism features Agent → applies to player-experience theories (Salen & Zimmerman), psychological-immersion theories, avatar/identity studies. **Test:** does this theory explain motive primarily via properties of the player-subject?

---

## 3. Realism — features ACT (GM-06) **[UNIQUE EXEGETICAL ANCHOR]**

**Diagnostic.** Features Act via the actualization-of-form-of-kind (entelechy) mechanism. Distinguishes from scenic-reduction (motion) and idealist agent-features. **The pipeline's unique EXEGETICAL anchor** — Burke himself ties Act to Aristotle/Aquinas.

| Philosopher | Pages | Burke's exegetical move | Exegesis |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Aristotle** | 227, 230-231, 249 | *Energeia* / actuality / entelechy as act-featuring. *In rebus* realism — Idea-not-generative; things-strive-toward-perfection-of-kind. *Metaphysics* IX + *Poetics* 6 + *Physics* I.6-7 + *De Anima* + *NE*. | **EXEGETICAL-DIRECT** |
| **Aquinas** | 227 + GM-06 main | *Actus* / *potentia* + agent-act ratio + existence-as-act-of-essence + soul-as-act-of-body. Ibn-Sina auxiliary-efficient-cause as agent/agency overlap. 'Rationalizer of the Christian drama.' | **EXEGETICAL-DIRECT** |
| **Plato** | GM-06 | Transcendent *ante rem* realism (Idea generative). Aristotle 'neutralizes' Platonist realism. |
| **Duns Scotus** | GM-06 | *Haecceitas* (thisness) as surface-nominalistic but tribal-familial-pattern-retaining; individual treated as a genus (*socratitas*). |
| **Stoics** (within realism) | GM-06 | *Hegemonikon* as reason-authority equation linking private rule and public rule. |
| **Christian theologians** | GM-06 | Transvaluation of suffering as act; willing-one's-subjection; martyrdom as act-of-self-sacrifice identical with sufferance. |
| **Ibn-Sina (Avicenna)** | GM-06 | Auxiliary-efficient-cause that lets Aquinas relate agent and agency without collapsing them. |
| **Occam** | GM-06 | Nominalist boundary; classification-first-by-individuals as departure from realism. |
| **Étienne Gilson** | GM-06 | Modern Thomist interlocutor; scholarly reconstruction of actus-essence apparatus. |

**Characteristic moves.** *Energeia* / actuality as defining-mark of the real · entelechy — each kind of thing striving to perfectly be the kind it is · form is the actus; existence as act of essence · soul as act of body · *in rebus* vs *ante rem* distinction.

**Dissertation game-studies deployment.** Realism features Act → applies to **ludology** (Aarseth, Juul, Frasca — gameplay-as-act-of-rule-following) and procedural-rhetoric (Bogost). **Test:** does this theory explain motive primarily via what-is-actually-done?

---

## 4. Pragmatism — features AGENCY (GM-07 first half)

**Diagnostic.** Action explained by medium that mediates it. Burke calls pragmatism the 'mediator-form' among the five featurings. Modern science's elimination of final cause raises Agency to ancestral term; money is paradigm Agency.

| Philosopher | Pages | Burke's exegetical move |
|---|---|---|
| **William James** | GM-07 | Method only; cash-value; menial services. Foregrounds method/instrument. *Varieties* engages mysticism as 'Sick Soul' from outside. |
| **John Dewey** | GM-07 + GM-00 p.xxi | Instrumentalism; *Experience and Nature*. Intelligence as instrument embodied in scientific method. 'Experience' and 'nature' as act/scene equivalents; continuity replaces separation. |
| **G. H. Mead** | GM-07 + GM-06 p.236 | *Philosophy of the Act*; the 'other' whose attitudes we dialectically include. Named 'philosophy of the act' yet analytical apparatus is agency-foregrounding. Attitude as 'beginning of acts.' |
| **Charles Peirce** | GM-07 background | Beliefs as rules for action; pragmatic-maxim grounds James/Dewey/Mead. |
| **P. W. Bridgman** | GM-07 | Operationalism; *Logic of Modern Physics*. **Limit-case**: writes about his purpose in eliminating the concept of purpose. The agency-purpose paradox at its sharpest. |
| **Aristotle** (incipient) | GM-07 p.276 | *Organon* as 'incipiently pragmatist' but subordinated under final cause. |
| **Emerson** | GM-07 background | Incipient pragmatism via *Nature*'s Commodity/Beauty/Language/Discipline sequence. |
| **Bentham** | GM-07 | Utilitarianism / 'fig-leaves' — quantifying agency through utility-calculus. |
| **Hegel** (cross-school) | GM-07 | *Vermittlung* (mediation) as incipient pragmatist agency-foregrounding. |
| **Marx** (cross-school) | GM-07 | Economic-conditions reading as form-laden, pragmatism-adjacent in stressing instrument/medium. |

**Characteristic moves.** Instrument-as-ancestor · documentary historiography · two principles of verification (James) · action-motion ambiguity straddled · corporate-entity-as-agent (Papini corridor; financial-page 'it') · money as cash-value-medium.

**Dissertation game-studies deployment.** Pragmatism features Agency → applies to **kinesthetic-immersion** theories, controller-studies, embodied-cognition (Gee, Sicart), procedural-rhetoric (mechanics-as-means). **Test:** does this theory explain motive primarily via the means/controller/rule-system?

---

## 5. Mysticism — features PURPOSE (GM-07 second half)

**Diagnostic.** Action explained by cosmic end toward which it is drawn. Burke's mark of mysticism is 'unity of the individual with some cosmic or universal purpose,' NOT mere unity. Pure Purpose collapses into the paradox-of-substance, into mechanism, into the negative.

| Philosopher | Pages | Burke's exegetical move |
|---|---|---|
| **Plotinus** | GM-07 | *Enneads* I.3 — journey to the Good, to the Primal-Principle. Mystic Upward Way; negative-theology paradigm. |
| **Plato** (within mysticism) | GM-07 | Good = One. Platonic mystical strain alongside realist strain. |
| **Bonaventura** | GM-07 | Christian mystical Purpose; mind's journey to God. |
| **Augustine** | GM-07 passing | Restless heart finds rest in God = unity with cosmic Purpose. |
| **Thomas à Kempis** | GM-07 | *Imitation of Christ* — 'In all things behold the end.' |
| **William James** (within mysticism) | GM-07 | *Varieties of Religious Experience* — Tolstoy's drought / 'Sick Soul.' Pragmatist-mystic crossover. |
| **Spinoza** (within mysticism strand) | GM-07 | Mystical strain in Oneness/Allness; *omnis determinatio est negatio* anchors *via negativa*. |
| **Bergson** | GM-07 | *Creative Evolution* — negative as function of desire; semi-mystical, semi-pragmatist. |
| **Aristotle** (near-but-not) | GM-07 | *Eudaimonia* as realistic-not-mystical synonym for Purpose. NEAR but NOT mystical. |
| **Kant** (mysticism crossover) | GM-07 | Synthetic unity of apperception as Mystical-Idealist crossover; transcendent als-ob ideas. |
| **Korzybski** | GM-07 | Upward Way as higher generalization; rites of desanctification. General Semantics' structural-differential as mystic apparatus despite anti-mystical surface. |
| **Huxley** | GM-07 | **Mysticism of Means** — Burke's specifically critiqued limit-case (pacifism). |
| **T. S. Eliot** | GM-07 | *Murder in the Cathedral*; *Little Gidding*. |
| **Shelley** | GM-07 | *Alastor* — reflexive journey. |
| **Dostoevsky** | GM-07 | Raskolnikov's 'representative' act. Existential-mystic Purpose. |
| **Nietzsche** | GM-07 | Eternal recurrence as mystic reflexive-doubling apparatus. |

**Characteristic moves.** Upward Way · mystic oxymoron / *docta ignorantia* · *via negativa* · reflexive doublings · mystic 'moment' / rebirth-grammar · demonic trinity (cloacal-mystical imagery) · Silence-and-Hunt biological substrate.

**Burke critique.** Pure Purpose passes into paradox-of-substance (compulsion, mechanism). Mysticism arrives at the same narrowing-of-circumference as materialism by absolutizing Purpose into fatality. Mysticism + idealism reinforce each other in the abstract Self. Mysticism-of-means (Huxley) is the critiqued limit-case.

**Dissertation game-studies deployment.** Mysticism features Purpose → applies to **narratology** (Murray, Jenkins), flow/affective theories, and **gamification** as cosmic-purpose rhetoric. **Test:** does this theory explain motive via narrative-arc / mastery-cosmos / affective-purpose-unification? Gamification's absolutized 'engagement' as pure-Purpose by Burke's paradox-of-purity flips into compulsion-loop critique.

---

## Rationalism (transitional crosscut)

Burke names Rationalism as cross-cutting all five terms by featuring method/structure. He declares his own *Grammar* 'rationalistic in this dialectical sense.' Canonical: Descartes (*Discourse on Method*), Spinoza (*Ethics more geometrico*), Leibniz (*Characteristica Universalis*), Hegel ('world is Reason'), Freud (great modern dialectician).

## Dissertation game-studies diagnostic apparatus

| Game-studies sub-school | Featured pentad term | Burke school analog |
|---|---|---|
| **Ludology** (Aarseth, Juul, Frasca) | Act | Realism — *in rebus* entelechy of gameplay-act |
| **Narratology** (Murray, Jenkins) | Scene + Purpose | Materialism + Mysticism — environmental storytelling + cyberdrama arc |
| **Embodied-cognition / Kinesthetic** (Gee, Sicart, Calleja) | Agency | Pragmatism — body/controller/rules-as-means |
| **Psychological immersion** (Salen & Zimmerman) | Agent | Idealism — properties of the player-subject |
| **Platform studies** (Bogost, Murray) | Scene | Materialism — platform constraints |
| **Procedural rhetoric** (Bogost) | Act + Agency | Realism + Pragmatism hybrid — mechanics-as-rhetoric |
| **Gamification critique** | Purpose (paradox-of-purity) | Mysticism (critiqued limit-case) — 'engagement' as compulsion-loop |
